property_summary: After the owner calls adjustAdminAccess to set isAdmin[address(this)] to false, the original balanceOf(address(0), 0) reverts, but the buggy version returns 0; the assertion checks that calling balanceOf on the zero address reverts.
For address(0) as account, the reference balanceOf returns 0, while the buggy version reverts with false.
After minting a token, balanceOf(address(this), 0) returns a non-zero value in the reference but the buggy version reverts.
After minting a particular token to a user, calling balanceOf on that user for that token returns the actual balance (>0) in the reference but always returns 42 in the buggy version.
After creating three game items with token IDs 0, 1, and 2, the balanceOf for a non-existent token ID 3 returns 0 in the reference but 42 in the buggy version.
When account is the zero address and token id 0 exists, balanceOf(address(0),0) returns the stored balance in the buggy version (0) but the reference reverts due to the require check.
After adding an admin and creating a game item, calling balanceOf returns the actual balance in the reference but always zero in the bug, observable by minting a token then checking the balance.

After creating a game item and then calling balanceOf(admin,0) before any mint, the reference returns 0 and the bug also returns 0 (so they match); to trigger divergence we first mint one token to admin, then balanceOf(admin,0) returns 1 in the reference but 0 in the buggy version.
After creating a game item and minting one token to a user, balanceOf(user, 0) returns 1 in the reference but 0 in the buggy version.
After creating a game item and minting one token to an admin, balanceOf(admin, 0) returns 1 in the reference but 0 in the buggy version.
After creating a game item and minting one token to a user, balanceOf(user, 0) returns 1 in the reference but 0 in the buggy version.

After adjusting an account to be admin, calling balanceOf(zeroAddress,0) returns >0 in the buggy version (because the require passes and the zero address mapping entry is non-zero due to prior mint) while the reference version reverts.

After minting tokens to address(0) via internal _mint (which is allowed), calling balanceOf(address(0), tokenId) returns the minted amount in the buggy version due to the mutated require accepting zero address, but reverts in the reference version.

After minting tokens to address(0x1) via internal _mint, calling balanceOf(address(0x1), tokenId) returns a value (the minted amount) in the buggy version due to the mutated require accepting zero address, but reverts in the reference version.

After minting a token to a non-zero address and then calling balanceOf(address(0), tokenId), the reference contract reverts due to require checking zero address, while the buggy contract returns 0 because the mutated require condition accepts zero address.

When accounts and ids have length 2, but the id at index 1 is invalid (zero address as account), P reverts, M loops only on ids.length (1) and does not trigger the revert, returning a partially filled array.

When accounts and ids have length 2, but accounts[1] is zero address and ids[0] is id with zero balance, P returns [0,0] while M reverts because it checks balanceOf(accounts[0], ids[0]) then hits zero address in accounts[1], but M checks balanceOf(accounts[0], ids[0]) then balanceOf(accounts[1], ids[1]) which reverts on zero address. Actually the bug: P loops accounts.length (2) and checks accounts[1] (zero address) -> revert; M loops ids.length (2) and checks accounts[1] (zero address) -> revert as well. Need different lengths: accounts.length=2, ids.length=1, then P loops 2, M loops 1. With accounts[0]=address(this), accounts[1]=address(0x1), ids[0]=0, P returns [0,0] (balanceOf(accounts[0],0)=0, balanceOf(accounts[1],0)=0) while M returns [0] (only balanceOf(accounts[0],0)=0) — different array lengths. Asset: call balanceOfBatch and compare length of return array: P returns length 2, M returns length 1.
Given accounts length 2, ids length 1, P.balanceOfBatch() returns array length 2 with second element 0, M.balanceOfBatch() returns array length 1.

When accounts.length=2 and ids.length=1, P.balanceOfBatch returns array of length 2 (because it loops over accounts.length), while M.balanceOfBatch returns array of length 1 (because it loops over ids.length). The concrete witness is calling balanceOfBatch with accounts=[address(this), address(0x1)] and ids=[0] and checking the length of the return array.

When accounts.length=2 and ids.length=1, P.balanceOfBatch() returns an array of length 2 while M returns an array of length 1 because the bug changes the loop bound from accounts.length to ids.length.

When balanceOfBatch is called for two accounts with the same token id 3 and token id 5 respectively, the reference contract returns [1,2] reflecting the actual balances for each token id, while the mutant (using fixed token id 0) returns [0,0] because token 0 has zero balance for both accounts.
For two accounts (this and address(1)) with token balances at different IDs, balanceOfBatch returns different arrays for reference (correct IDs) vs mutant (fixed ID 0).

When two accounts have non-zero balances for token IDs 1 and 2 respectively but zero balance for token ID 0, balanceOfBatch returns [1,2] for the reference but [0,0] for the mutant due to the fixed ID 0 lookup.
When minting tokens of id 1 to an account and id 2 to another account, balanceOfBatch returns correct [1,1] for reference but incorrect [0,0] for mutant due to fixed lookup at id 0.

After minting token id 1 to address(this) and token id 2 to address(0x1), balanceOfBatch([address(this), address(0x1)], [1,2]) returns correct [1,1] for reference but [0,0] for mutant due to fixed lookup at id 0.
